summary: The prepared source already routes Qwen 3.8 PLE weight_scale checkpoint tensors into their registered buffers before the generic non-unit unknown-scale assertion. A regression using the reported tensor name and value verifies that behavior; no duplicate production fix was added.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-7b4da83353d7/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_weight_loading.py::test_loads_non_unit_ple_embedding_weight_scale (with weight_scale temporarily removed from the PLE buffer allowlist)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before sensitivity: the actual load_weights path reproduced the issue's exact AssertionError and value when the current PLE scale routing was removed (1 failed).
Passing-after/current-source regression and independent boundaries: exact reported non-unit scale copy/loaded bookkeeping, mismatched-shape rejection, and unrelated-scale non-claiming (3 passed).
On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, the loader copied the reported FP32 value to a GPU BF16 buffer; its value exactly equaled an independent CPU BF16 conversion and the buffer was marked loaded.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-; GPU value 0.00019931793212890625 equaled the independent CPU BF16 reference and the checkpoint name was marked loaded.
remaining_limitations: The Qwen 3.8 checkpoint weights were unavailable, so no full model load, serving, semantic-accuracy, or distributed reproduction was performed. The tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify this Qwen-specific loader path. No native code changed.
